summary:
​High-Level Summary (Elevator Pitch)
A turn-based, interactive web simulator that challenges users to manage a Martian outpost. By balancing critical life-support resources—power, oxygen, and crew morale—against random crisis events, players practically engage with real-world NASA engineering concepts to survive a 14-Sol mission.
​Detailed Project Description
To address the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge, our team developed a lightweight, gamified web application utilizing HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript. The core engine relies on a Sol-based (Martian day) turn system where commanders must allocate limited action points to maintain base subsystem integrity.
details:
Key features include:

  • ​Resource Balancing Algorithm: Simulates the constant depletion and generation of Power, Oxygen, and Morale based on user decisions and environmental factors.
  • ​Subsystem Engineering Deck: Features interactive modules modeled on real NASA technology, including the MOXIE O₂ Plant, Kilopower RTG, and the Veggie Hydroponics system.
  • ​Crisis Event Engine: Randomly generates anomalies like micrometeorite showers and global dust storms, forcing users to adapt their power routing and life-support strategies under pressure.
  • ​Educational Integration: Seamlessly weaves in NASA tech flashcards and mission facts, rewarding users with resource boosts when they learn about planetary surface operations.

​The application is deployed via Netlify for instant, cross-device accessibility without requiring any app store downloads or complex installations.

​AI Tool Disclosure

In accordance with the hackathon guidelines, generative AI tools (Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, and OpenAI ChatGPT) were utilized to brainstorm system architecture, verify mathematical state-space logic for the resource economy, and synthesize raw NASA datasets into accessible game mechanics and educational flashcards.
